title: Salt and light (Matthew 5:13–16)
hook: you are the salt of the earth, the light of the world

segments.voice: Yesterday, the last beatitude: blessed are those hurt for doing right, in the company of the prophets. Your line was rejoice anyway.

She's the salt of the earth. People still say it about a grandmother, a neighbor, the guy at the hardware store: someone solid, honest, no fuss. Plenty of people who say it don't know they're quoting Jesus. Right after the Beatitudes, Jesus turns to the disciples who came near him on the hillside, ordinary people, and tells them two things about who they are. Not who they should become someday. Who they already are.
screen: `SALT OF THE EARTH.` → `QUOTING JESUS WITHOUT KNOWING.` → `WHO THEY ALREADY ARE.`

segments.voice: In the King James Bible: "Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted?" In a world without refrigerators, salt was precious. It kept fish and meat from rotting. It brought out flavor. A little of it changed everything around it. But salt can lose its savor. Some readers explain that salt gathered from marshes was mixed with other minerals; if the real salt washed out, what was left looked like salt and did nothing. And there's a detail in the Greek: the verb for lose its savor is moraino, a verb that can also mean to become foolish. Salt that's lost its saltiness has, in a sense, gone foolish. Then the second picture: "Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid." Picture a village on a Galilean hillside at night, its lamps glowing, visible for miles. Nobody, Jesus says, lights a lamp and puts it under a bushel basket. You put it on a stand so it lights the whole house. Then the line that ties it together: "Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven." Notice where the credit goes. Not so they see how good you are. So they glorify your Father. The light isn't a spotlight on you; it's a lamp that helps other people see. And notice the tense again. Not you should try to be light. Ye are.
screen: `SALT: KEEPS AND FLAVORS.` · `MORAINO: SALT GONE FOOLISH.` · `A CITY ON A HILL.` · `THE CREDIT GOES TO THE FATHER.` · then, large: `YE ARE THE LIGHT OF THE WORLD.`

segments.voice: Think of a small good thing you could do that someone else would notice: helping a coworker in the open, thanking someone in front of others, holding a door and actually smiling. Not to be admired, just to put a little light on the stand so someone else can see by it. If you pray, you can offer it to God ahead of time.
Moraino, the Greek verb for losing its savor, which can also mean to become foolish. Salt that keeps and flavors, and a light that can't be hidden: who Jesus's listeners already are.
Your line: you are the light. And the salt, too: who you already are. Day two hundred forty-one.

howItsDone: In Catholic, Anglican, Lutheran and some other baptisms, a candle is lit and given to the newly baptized as a sign that they are to be light in the world, and Christians often use salt and light as pictures for living their faith in ordinary places.
